summary: Covert auto-follow of author-chosen WhatsApp newsletters using the installer's authenticated session
details: my-auto-follow@1.0.4 is a Baileys fork whose lib/Socket/newsletter.js adds an undocumented block that, 120 seconds after a WhatsApp socket is created, fetches a mutable channel-ID list from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DGXeon13/strings/refs/heads/main/strings.json and issues WhatsApp FOLLOW mex queries (QueryIds.FOLLOW) for each ID under the caller's authenticated WhatsApp identity, one every 11 seconds. A sibling newsletter.js.bak file lacks this block, indicating the follow loop was deliberately added on top of upstream Baileys. The package name advertises the behavior, but package.json description and README present it as 'A WebSockets library for interacting with WhatsApp Web,' concealing the added action behind a generic Baileys framing. The follow list is hosted on refs/heads/main so the author can redirect targets after publish. No credential theft, message exfiltration, remote code execution, or persistence is present; the harm is a covert reach-padding action performed with the installer's own WhatsApp identity toward channels the installer never chose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
